## How it is organised

Every entry is tagged on two axes. The first says how the work defines populism. The second says what populism is studied alongside.

::: {.pv-axes}

::: {.pv-axis}
### Approaches to populism

- Ideational: populism as a thin ideology (Mudde)
- Discursive (Laclau, the Essex school)
- Political-strategic (Weyland)
- Performative or stylistic (Moffitt)
- Socio-cultural (Ostiguy)
- Economic or structural
- Measurement and methods: how populism is measured
- Other or multiple
:::

::: {.pv-axis}
### Populism and…

- Foreign policy
- Defence and security
- The international sphere: the EU, international organisations, multilateralism
- Parties, leaders and movements: the supply side
- Voters and attitudes: the demand side
- Populists in government
- Spatial populism: geography, urban–rural divides, regions
- Economy and welfare
- Media and communication
- Gender
- Religion
- Migration
- Democracy and institutions
- Other
:::

:::

Entries can also be filtered by region, country, method, type of publication, year, journal and open access.

## What goes in

Peer-reviewed articles, books, book chapters, and selected policy and working papers on populism, in English. Inclusion is an editorial decision. It rests on two tests: relevance to populism as a concept or to populist actors, and scholarly standard.

## What each entry gives you

The full citation, the abstract as published, a link to the DOI or to an open-access copy, the tags on both axes, and a BibTeX reference in one click. PopuliVerse links to papers. It does not host them.

## Suggest a paper

Is something missing? Send the title or the DOI, and a line on why it belongs here.

## The Zotero group

The Library lives in a public Zotero group called "PopuliVerse Library". Anyone can read it and use it in their own Zotero. Scholars who contribute regularly are invited to join it as editors.
